message.content:
The exact count of all legal positions in chess is still unknown, but it’s been estimated to be on the order of **10⁴³**.  
If you’re asking about the number of possible *games* (i.e., sequences of legal moves from start to finish), the classic estimate is the **Shannon number**, roughly **10¹²⁰**.

So:

| What you’re counting | Rough estimate |
|----------------------|----------------|
| Legal positions (arrangements of pieces on the board) | ~10⁴³ |
| Possible games (full move sequences) | ~10¹²⁰ |

These figures come from combinatorial analyses and Monte‑Carlo simulations; the true numbers are not known exactly because the search space is astronomically large.
